questions.hint: Solve in two steps: first add, then subtract.

questions.subject: MATH
questions.question: Franz buys 4 pens at 11 pesos each. What is the total cost?
questions.explanation: Total = 11 x 4 = 44 pesos.
questions.hint: Total cost = price each x number of items.

questions.subject: MATH
questions.question: Elsa had 35 cards, won 31 more, then gave 12 to a friend. How many cards does Elsa have now?
questions.hint: Solve in two steps: first add, then subtract.

questions.subject: MATH
questions.question: Three test scores are 10, 12, and 17. What is the average score?
questions.hint: Average = sum of scores / number of scores.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Which of these is an example of a solid?
questions.answer: Ice cube
questions.explanation: An ice cube keeps its own shape and volume, which are the defining traits of a solid.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: What is the process called when a solid changes into a liquid?
questions.answer: Melting
questions.explanation: Melting happens when a solid absorbs heat and its particles break free from fixed positions.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: What is the process called when a gas changes into a liquid?
questions.answer: Condensation
questions.explanation: Condensation happens when gas particles lose energy and come together as a liquid, like dew forming.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Which state of matter is water at -20 degrees Celsius under normal pressure?
questions.answer: Solid
questions.explanation: Below 0 degrees Celsius (its freezing point), water becomes ice - a solid.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: What is the process called when a liquid changes into a gas?
questions.answer: Evaporation
questions.explanation: Evaporation occurs when liquid particles gain enough energy to escape into the air as gas.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: At what temperature does pure water freeze under normal pressure?
questions.answer: 0 degrees Celsius
questions.explanation: Pure water freezes at 0 degrees Celsius and boils at 100 degrees Celsius at normal atmospheric pressure.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Recall: Which observation BEST shows that air is matter in the gas state?
choices: An inflated balloon weighs slightly more than a deflated one
questions.answer: An inflated balloon weighs slightly more than a deflated one
questions.explanation: Air has mass and takes up space - the inflated balloon is slightly heavier because it contains compressed gas.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Recall: Which container property best proves that a liquid has definite volume?
choices: The amount of liquid stays the same when poured between containers
The liquid always fills the whole container
questions.answer: The amount of liquid stays the same when poured between containers
questions.explanation: When you pour a liquid from one container to another, its shape changes but the volume (amount) stays the same.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Which of these is an example of a gas?
questions.answer: Oxygen
questions.explanation: Oxygen spreads out to fill any container, which is the behavior of a gas.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Recall: Which of the following is NOT a state of matter discussed in this lesson?
questions.answer: Energy
questions.explanation: Solid, liquid, and gas are states of matter; energy is not a state of matter.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Which of these substances is in the liquid state at room temperature?
questions.answer: Alcohol
questions.explanation: At room temperature alcohol is a liquid, iron and sand are solids, and oxygen is a gas.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Ice melting in a glass of juice is an example of which process?
questions.answer: Melting
questions.explanation: The warm juice transfers heat to the ice, so the solid ice changes into liquid water.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Which of these is an example of a liquid?
questions.answer: Water
questions.explanation: Water flows and takes the shape of its container while keeping a fixed volume, so it is a liquid.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Mothballs shrinking inside a closet over time is an example of ____.
questions.answer: Sublimation
questions.explanation: Mothballs change directly from solid to gas, slowly shrinking - this is sublimation.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Recall: A balloon filled with air expands to fill the whole balloon. This shows that gas ____.
questions.answer: Fills all available space
questions.explanation: Gas particles spread out until they occupy the entire space of the container.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: What kind of motion does a spinning electric fan show?
questions.answer: Rotational motion
questions.explanation: Rotational motion is movement around an axis or center point, like fan blades spinning around the hub.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: The Earth rotating once every 24 hours around its axis is ____.
questions.answer: Rotational motion
questions.explanation: Earth spins around its own axis, which causes day and night - rotational motion.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: When a door swings open on its hinges, the door shows ____.
questions.answer: Rotational motion around the hinges
questions.explanation: Every point on the door moves in an arc around the hinge line - rotation around the hinges.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: The second hand of a watch completes one full ____ every minute.
questions.answer: Rotation
questions.explanation: The second hand rotates once around the dial each minute.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: The wheels of a moving bicycle are best described as showing ____.
questions.answer: Both translational and rotational motion
questions.explanation: The wheels spin around their axles (rotational) while traveling forward with the bicycle (translational).
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Which measurement describes how fast an object moves from one point to another?
questions.answer: Speed
questions.explanation: Speed measures how fast an object covers distance over time.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Recall: A satellite dish slowly turning to face a satellite shows ____.
questions.answer: Rotational motion
questions.explanation: The dish rotates around its mount to track the satellite.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Which observation proves that a wheel has rotational motion?
choices: A spot painted on the rim moves in a circle
The wheel makes a straight line
questions.answer: A spot painted on the rim moves in a circle
questions.explanation: A marked point on the rim traces a circle around the axle, proving rotation.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: What kind of motion does a book sliding straight across a table show?
questions.answer: Translational motion
questions.explanation: Translational motion is movement in which every part of an object moves the same distance in the same direction, like a sliding book.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Which scenario shows an object in translational motion only?
choices: A sled sliding down a straight slope
questions.answer: A sled sliding down a straight slope
questions.explanation: The sled moves straight down the slope without spinning, so it shows translational motion only.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: A Ferris wheel turning slowly is an example of ____.
questions.answer: Rotational motion
questions.explanation: The wheel rotates around its central axle - rotational motion.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Which object shows pure rotational motion while staying in one place?
questions.answer: A merry-go-round in operation
questions.explanation: A merry-go-round spins around its center while its base stays in the same place.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: A windmill turning in the wind shows ____.
questions.answer: Rotational motion
questions.explanation: The windmill's blades rotate around its central shaft.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Recall: A box pushed so that it slides and then also starts to tumble shows ____.
choices: A combination of translational and rotational motion
questions.answer: A combination of translational and rotational motion
questions.explanation: Sliding gives translation; tumbling adds rotation - both motions combined.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: In translational motion, all parts of the object move ____.
choices: The same distance in the same direction
questions.answer: The same distance in the same direction
questions.explanation: Translation shifts the whole object, so every part travels the same distance and direction.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Doubling the area over which the same force acts will ____ the pressure.
questions.answer: Halve
questions.explanation: Since P = F / A, spreading the same force over twice the area halves the pressure.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: In hydraulic brakes, the master cylinder ____.
choices: Creates pressure in the brake fluid when the pedal is pressed
questions.answer: Creates pressure in the brake fluid when the pedal is pressed
questions.explanation: The master cylinder pushes on the brake fluid, creating the pressure transmitted to the wheel cylinders.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Which statement best summarizes force multiplication in hydraulics?
choices: Area has no effect on force
A small force over a small area can produce a large force over a large area
A large force is needed at both pistons
questions.answer: A small force over a small area can produce a large force over a large area
questions.explanation: Equal pressure acting on a larger area yields a larger force - the essence of hydraulic force multiplication.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Recall: A force of 75 N acts on an area of 5 m2. What pressure is produced?
questions.answer: 15 Pa
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: A nurse presses a syringe plunger and fluid comes out the needle. This best illustrates ____.
choices: Pressure in a confined fluid pushing fluid out through an opening
questions.answer: Pressure in a confined fluid pushing fluid out through an opening
questions.explanation: Pressing the plunger raises pressure inside the confined fluid, forcing it out through the narrow needle.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: A force of 90 N produces a pressure of 10 Pa. Over what area is it applied?
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: A water pressure of 40 Pa acts on a piston of area 5 m2. The force on the piston is ____.
questions.explanation: F = P x A = 40 Pa x 5 m2 = 200 N.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Pascal's Principle applies mainly to ____.
questions.answer: Confined (enclosed) fluids
questions.explanation: The principle works for fluids - liquids and gases - that are confined inside a closed system.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: What happens to the pressure at all points of a sealed water tank when a pump adds 50 Pa?
choices: Pressure rises only near the pump
questions.answer: Pressure rises by 50 Pa everywhere
questions.explanation: Added pressure in a confined fluid is transmitted equally, so every point gains the same 50 Pa.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: A force of 240 N produces a pressure of 60 Pa. Over what area is it applied?
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Which device works based on Pascal's Principle?
questions.answer: Hydraulic jack
questions.explanation: A hydraulic jack multiplies force using confined fluid pressure, exactly as Pascal's Principle describes.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: What is the SI unit of pressure?
questions.answer: Pascal (Pa)
questions.explanation: Pressure is measured in pascals; 1 Pa = 1 N/m2.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: One pascal is equal to ____.
questions.answer: 1 newton per square meter
questions.explanation: By definition, 1 Pa = 1 N/m2.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: A confined fluid at 250 Pa pushes on a piston of area 3 m2. What force results?
questions.explanation: F = P x A = 250 Pa x 3 m2 = 750 N.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Doubling the force applied to a confined fluid (same area) will ____ the pressure.
questions.answer: Double
questions.explanation: Since P = F / A, doubling force with the same area doubles the pressure.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Why are hydraulic systems filled with liquid rather than gas for lifting heavy loads?
choices: Liquids are nearly incompressible, so pressure transfers efficiently
questions.answer: Liquids are nearly incompressible, so pressure transfers efficiently
questions.explanation: Liquids barely compress, so nearly all applied pressure is transmitted to do work; gases would compress and absorb much of it.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Recall: If 300 N is applied to a piston with area 0.5 m2, the pressure created is ____.
questions.answer: 600 Pa
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: A confined fluid at 200 Pa pushes on a piston of area 6 m2. What force results?
questions.explanation: F = P x A = 200 Pa x 6 m2 = 1200 N.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: A force of 20 N is applied over an area of 4 m2. What is the pressure?
questions.answer: 5 Pa
questions.explanation: P = F / A = 20 N / 4 m2 = 5 Pa (pascals).
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: A force of 120 N produces a pressure of 60 Pa. Over what area is it applied?
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Which ancient scientist is Archimedes' Principle named after?
questions.answer: Archimedes of Syracuse
questions.explanation: Archimedes of Syracuse, a Greek mathematician, discovered the principle of buoyancy.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Which statement about Archimedes' Principle is FALSE?
choices: Buoyancy works in liquids and gases
Buoyant force depends on the object's color
Denser fluids give more buoyant force
Buoyant force equals the weight of displaced fluid
questions.answer: Buoyant force depends on the object's color
questions.explanation: Color has no effect on buoyancy; buoyant force depends on displaced fluid weight, not appearance.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Recall: Which object will most likely FLOAT in water?
questions.answer: A wooden block
questions.explanation: Wood is less dense than water, so the buoyant force can support it; the metal and glass objects are denser and sink.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Recall: A 5 N toy boat floats in a tub. How much water does it displace by weight?
questions.answer: 5 N of water
questions.explanation: For floating objects, displaced water weight equals the object's weight - 5 N.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Recall: When you push a ball underwater and let go, it pops up because ____.
choices: The buoyant force is greater than the ball's weight
questions.answer: The buoyant force is greater than the ball's weight
questions.explanation: The ball displaces water weighing more than the ball itself, so the net force pushes it up.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: If an object displaces 8 N of water and weighs 8 N, it will ____.
choices: Rise out of the water completely
questions.answer: Float (remain balanced in the water)
questions.explanation: Buoyant force equals weight, so the object is balanced - it floats without sinking or rising further.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Recall: Objects less dense than water generally ____.
questions.answer: Float
questions.explanation: Lower density than water means buoyant force can balance the object's weight, so it floats.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: A balloon underwater is squeezed smaller as it goes deeper. Its buoyant force ____.
choices: Decreases because it displaces less water
questions.answer: Decreases because it displaces less water
questions.explanation: Smaller volume means less displaced water, so buoyant force drops.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Objects denser than water generally ____.
questions.answer: Sink
questions.explanation: If an object's density exceeds water's, its weight beats the buoyant force, so it sinks.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Recall: When a cargo ship moves from a river into the sea, it rides slightly higher because ____.
choices: Sea water is denser than fresh water
questions.answer: Sea water is denser than fresh water
questions.explanation: Denser sea water provides more buoyant force per volume, so the ship needs to displace less water and rides higher.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: A submerged object feels lighter because ____.
choices: Buoyant force pushes up against its weight
questions.answer: Buoyant force pushes up against its weight
questions.explanation: The upward buoyant force offsets part of the object's weight.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Which factor increases the buoyant force on a submerged object?
questions.answer: Greater volume of the object
questions.explanation: More volume means more fluid displaced, which means greater buoyant force.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: A boat carrying cargo sits lower in the water because ____.
choices: It displaces more water to support the extra weight
questions.answer: It displaces more water to support the extra weight
questions.explanation: Extra weight requires extra buoyant force, so the boat sinks deeper and displaces more water.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Recall: A submarine surfaces by ____.
choices: Pumping water out of its ballast tanks to become lighter
questions.answer: Pumping water out of its ballast tanks to become lighter
questions.explanation: Expelling ballast water reduces weight below the buoyant force, so the submarine rises.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Dead Sea swimmers float very easily because the water ____.
questions.answer: Is extremely salty and dense
questions.explanation: Very high salt content makes Dead Sea water dense, producing a large buoyant force that keeps swimmers high on the surface.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Who discovered the electron using cathode ray tubes?
questions.answer: J.J. Thomson
questions.explanation: J.J. Thomson identified the electron in 1897, showing atoms contain smaller charged particles.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Who created the first successful vaccine, against smallpox?
questions.answer: Edward Jenner
questions.explanation: Edward Jenner developed the smallpox vaccine in 1796, the world's first successful vaccine.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Recall: Who proposed the theory of evolution by natural selection?
questions.answer: Charles Darwin
questions.explanation: Charles Darwin proposed evolution by natural selection in his 1859 book On the Origin of Species.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Who is considered the founder of modern nursing and used statistics to improve hospital care?
questions.answer: Florence Nightingale
questions.explanation: Florence Nightingale transformed nursing and pioneered statistical graphics to reduce hospital deaths.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Who proposed continental drift, the idea that continents slowly move?
questions.answer: Alfred Wegener
questions.explanation: Alfred Wegener proposed continental drift in 1912; plate tectonics later confirmed his idea.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Who discovered electromagnetic induction, the principle behind generators?
questions.answer: Michael Faraday
questions.explanation: Michael Faraday discovered electromagnetic induction in 1831 - changing magnetic fields can induce electric current.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Who is called the 'Father of Genetics' for his pea plant experiments?
questions.answer: Gregor Mendel
questions.explanation: Gregor Mendel's pea plant experiments in the 1860s revealed the basic laws of inheritance.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Who is known as the 'Father of Medicine'?
questions.answer: Hippocrates
questions.explanation: Hippocrates of ancient Greece is called the Father of Medicine; doctors still take a version of his oath.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Who developed the alternating current (AC) electrical system?
questions.answer: Nikola Tesla
questions.explanation: Nikola Tesla championed and developed the AC system that powers homes and industries today.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Who discovered the circulation of blood through the body?
questions.answer: William Harvey
questions.explanation: William Harvey described the full circulation of blood pumped by the heart in 1628.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Who developed the polio vaccine in the 1950s?
questions.answer: Jonas Salk
questions.explanation: Jonas Salk created the first successful inactivated polio vaccine, announced in 1955.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Which scientist improved the telescope and observed the moons of Jupiter?
questions.answer: Galileo Galilei
questions.explanation: Galileo improved the telescope and in 1610 observed four moons orbiting Jupiter, supporting the idea that not everything orbits Earth.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Who proposed the model of the atom with electrons in fixed energy levels?
questions.answer: Niels Bohr
questions.explanation: Niels Bohr proposed in 1913 that electrons orbit the nucleus in fixed energy levels.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Who proposed the quantum theory that energy comes in discrete packets (quanta)?
questions.answer: Max Planck
questions.explanation: Max Planck proposed in 1900 that energy is emitted in discrete packets called quanta, founding quantum theory.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Who discovered natural radioactivity in uranium?
questions.answer: Henri Becquerel
questions.explanation: Henri Becquerel discovered radioactivity in 1896 when uranium salts fogged photographic plates.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Recall: Which state of matter is water at 120 degrees Celsius under normal pressure?
questions.answer: Gas
questions.explanation: Above 100 degrees Celsius (its boiling point at normal pressure), water exists as water vapor, a gas.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Butter melting in a hot pan is an example of ____.
choices: A gas changing into a liquid
A solid changing into a gas
A liquid changing into a solid
A solid changing into a liquid
questions.answer: A solid changing into a liquid
questions.explanation: Heat from the pan makes the solid butter melt into liquid - a solid-to-liquid change.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Which change of state happens when wet clothes dry under the sun?
questions.answer: Liquid to gas
questions.explanation: Heat from the sun turns the liquid water in the clothes into water vapor, which escapes into the air.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Water boiling in a kettle changes from which state to which state?
questions.answer: Liquid to gas
questions.explanation: Boiling gives liquid water enough energy to become water vapor, a gas.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: When you squeeze a sponge filled with air, the air inside can be compressed because ____.
choices: Gas particles have large spaces between them
questions.answer: Gas particles have large spaces between them
questions.explanation: The spaces between gas particles allow gases to be compressed into a smaller volume.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Which statement about solids is TRUE?
choices: Solid particles vibrate in fixed positions
Solids take the shape of their container
questions.answer: Solid particles vibrate in fixed positions
questions.explanation: Solid particles cannot travel around; they only vibrate while staying in place, giving solids a fixed shape.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Which state of matter has a definite shape and a definite volume?
questions.answer: Solid
questions.explanation: Solids keep both a fixed shape and a fixed volume because their particles are packed tightly together.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: When water vapor in clouds turns into raindrops, the process is ____.
questions.answer: Condensation
questions.explanation: Water vapor (gas) cools in clouds and condenses into liquid water droplets that fall as rain.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Water droplets forming on the outside of a cold glass show which process?
questions.answer: Condensation
questions.explanation: Water vapor in the air cools on the cold surface and changes into liquid droplets - condensation.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Which state of matter has neither a definite shape nor a definite volume?
questions.answer: Gas
questions.explanation: Gas particles move freely and spread out to fill the entire container, so gases have no fixed shape or volume.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: What is the main difference between evaporation and boiling?
choices: They are exactly the same process
Evaporation happens at the surface at any temperature while boiling happens throughout the liquid at a fixed temperature
Boiling happens only at the surface
Evaporation happens only in the freezer
questions.answer: Evaporation happens at the surface at any temperature while boiling happens throughout the liquid at a fixed temperature
questions.explanation: Evaporation is a slow surface process at any temperature; boiling is rapid vapor formation throughout the liquid at its boiling point.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Particles of which state of matter have strong attraction that holds them in a fixed arrangement?
questions.answer: Solid
questions.explanation: Strong particle attraction in solids locks them into a fixed, orderly arrangement.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Which process removes heat from a substance?
questions.answer: Freezing
questions.explanation: Freezing happens when heat is removed from a liquid until it becomes a solid.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Cooking oil poured from a bottle into a pan shows that liquids ____.
choices: Take the shape of the container
questions.answer: Take the shape of the container
questions.explanation: The oil flows and adopts the shape of the pan while keeping the same volume - classic liquid behavior.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: In which state of matter are particles packed most closely together?
questions.answer: Solid
questions.explanation: Solid particles vibrate in fixed positions and are the most tightly packed of the three states.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Which type of motion is mainly responsible for day and night?
questions.answer: Rotational motion of the Earth
questions.explanation: Earth's rotation on its axis makes different sides face the Sun, producing day and night.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: A hockey puck sliding across the ice in a straight line shows ____.
questions.answer: Translational motion
questions.explanation: The puck glides in a straight line from one point to another - translational motion.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Vibrating guitar strings show which kind of motion?
questions.answer: Oscillating (vibrational) motion
questions.explanation: The strings vibrate rapidly back and forth around a resting position - oscillating motion.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Motion of an object around a fixed point in a circular path is called ____.
questions.answer: Rotational motion
questions.explanation: Circular movement around a fixed point or axis defines rotational motion.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Recall: Which example shows translational motion in a curved path?
choices: A car driving along a curved road
questions.answer: A car driving along a curved road

questions.question: A drill bit boring into wood shows ____.
questions.answer: Rotational motion

questions.subject: SCIENCE

A picture hanging on a wall

questions.explanation: The rolling bowling ball moves forward (translational) and spins (rotational) at the same time.

Absorbed by the container walls only

Air makes the fluid too heavy
Air compresses, so pressure would not be transmitted efficiently

choices: Pressure is transmitted through the confined paste in all directions

questions.question: Which scientist is Pascal's Principle named after?

questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Which is TRUE about the pressure at the input and output pistons of an ideal hydraulic lift?
choices: Pressure is zero at the output
The pressure is the same at both pistons
Pressure is higher at the input
Pressure is higher at the output

questions.explanation: Pascal's Principle transmits the pressure undiminished, so both pistons experience the same pressure.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Hydraulic car brakes use Pascal's Principle to ____.
choices: Transmit brake pedal force through brake fluid to all wheels
questions.answer: Transmit brake pedal force through brake fluid to all wheels
questions.explanation: Pressing the pedal creates pressure in the brake fluid, which is transmitted equally to push brake pistons at each wheel.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: A force of 50 N produces a pressure of 10 Pa. What area is the force applied to?
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.question: Which fluid property makes Pascal's Principle work well in hydraulics?
questions.answer: Incompressibility of liquids
questions.explanation: Because liquids barely compress, applied pressure is transmitted almost completely through the system.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: In Pascal's Principle, when pressure is transmitted through a confined fluid, it ____.
choices: Stays the same at every point

questions.explanation: The transmitted pressure is undiminished - equal at every point in the confined fluid.

questions.question: A force of 120 N produces a pressure of 40 Pa. Over what area is it applied?

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Recall: Excavator arms are moved by ____ applying Pascal's Principle.

questions.explanation: Hydraulic cylinders use confined fluid under pressure to push and pull the excavator's arms with great force.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Which formula expresses pressure?
questions.answer: Pressure = Force / Area
questions.explanation: Pressure is force spread over an area: P = F / A.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: A force of 60 N produces a pressure of 20 Pa. Over what area is it applied?
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: A sharp knife cuts easily because the thin edge ____.
choices: Concentrates force on a very small area, creating high pressure

questions.explanation: The same push over a tiny edge area produces very high pressure, so the knife cuts easily.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Wide shoulder straps on a heavy backpack are comfortable because they ____.
choices: Spread the force over a larger area, reducing pressure
Increase the pressure on the shoulders
questions.answer: Spread the force over a larger area, reducing pressure
questions.explanation: Larger contact area means lower pressure on your shoulders (P = F / A), so the bag feels more comfortable.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: The apparent weight of an object underwater is ____ its true weight in air.
questions.answer: Less than
questions.explanation: Buoyant force partially supports the object, so its measured (apparent) weight underwater is less.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Archimedes' Principle states that an object in a fluid experiences an upward buoyant force equal to ____.
choices: The weight of the fluid it displaces
The weight of the object itself
questions.answer: The weight of the fluid it displaces
questions.explanation: The buoyant force on a submerged or floating object equals the weight of the fluid displaced by the object.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Archimedes' Principle applies to ____.
questions.answer: Both liquids and gases
questions.explanation: Buoyancy occurs in all fluids - liquids and gases alike (ships in water, balloons in air).
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: An object exactly as dense as water will ____.
questions.answer: Hover (stay suspended) in the water
questions.explanation: Equal densities mean weight and buoyant force balance at any depth.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Recall: An ice cube floats in a glass of water because ____.
choices: Ice is less dense than liquid water
questions.answer: Ice is less dense than liquid water
questions.explanation: Frozen water is less dense than liquid water, so the buoyant force supports the ice cube.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Buoyant force acts in which direction?
questions.answer: Upward, opposite to gravity
questions.explanation: Buoyant force always pushes upward against the downward pull of gravity.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Hot air balloons rise because ____.
choices: Heated air inside is less dense than the surrounding cool air
Helium is required in all balloons
questions.answer: Heated air inside is less dense than the surrounding cool air
questions.explanation: Hot air is less dense, so the balloon displaces cooler air weighing more than the balloon system - buoyancy lifts it.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: An object floats when the buoyant force is ____ the object's weight.
questions.answer: Equal to or greater than
questions.explanation: Floating occurs when the upward buoyant force balances or exceeds the downward weight of the object.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: A submarine dives by ____.
choices: Taking water into ballast tanks to increase its weight
questions.answer: Taking water into ballast tanks to increase its weight
questions.explanation: Flooding ballast tanks makes the submarine heavier than the water it displaces, so it sinks; pumping water out lets it rise.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: A stone displaces 2 N of water when fully submerged. What buoyant force acts on it?
questions.answer: 2 N
questions.explanation: By Archimedes' Principle, buoyant force equals the weight of displaced fluid - 2 N.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Which instrument measures whether milk has been watered down using buoyancy?
questions.answer: A lactometer (hydrometer type)
questions.explanation: A lactometer floats higher in denser pure milk, revealing added water.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Recall: According to legend, Archimedes used his principle to check whether a crown was ____.
choices: Pure gold or mixed with cheaper metal
questions.answer: Pure gold or mixed with cheaper metal
questions.explanation: By comparing water displacement of the crown with equal weights of pure gold, Archimedes could detect lighter mixed metals.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Why does a steel ship float even though steel sinks in water?
choices: The ship's shape displaces a large volume of water, creating enough buoyant force
questions.answer: The ship's shape displaces a large volume of water, creating enough buoyant force
questions.explanation: The hollow hull displaces a huge amount of water; the weight of that displaced water equals or exceeds the ship's weight, so it floats.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Which object will most likely SINK in water?
questions.answer: A metal coin
questions.explanation: The coin is denser than water, so its weight exceeds the buoyant force and it sinks.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: A hydrometer is a device that uses buoyancy to measure ____.
questions.answer: The density of a liquid
questions.explanation: A hydrometer floats higher in denser liquids, letting us read liquid density directly.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Who wrote the influential anatomy book 'De humani corporis fabrica' based on dissections?
questions.answer: Andreas Vesalius

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Recall: Which inventor is most associated with the practical incandescent light bulb and phonograph?

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Who measured the speed of light accurately using rotating mirrors in the 1800s?

Isaac Newton measured it with candles only
Galileo measured it exactly with lanterns

questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Which ancient Greek philosopher classified animals and laid early foundations of biology?
questions.answer: Aristotle
questions.explanation: Aristotle systematically observed and classified animals, influencing biology for centuries.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Who pioneered wireless radio communication over long distances?
questions.answer: Guglielmo Marconi

questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Recall: Who discovered penicillin, the first true antibiotic?
questions.answer: Alexander Fleming
questions.explanation: Alexander Fleming discovered penicillin in 1928 when mold killed bacteria in one of his culture plates.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Recall: Which scientist won Nobel Prizes in both Physics and Chemistry for work on radioactivity?
questions.answer: Marie Curie

questions.question: Who discovered the neutron in 1932?
questions.answer: James Chadwick

questions.question: Which physicist discovered X-rays?
questions.answer: Wilhelm Roentgen
questions.explanation: Wilhelm Roentgen discovered X-rays in 1895 and took the first X-ray photograph of his wife's hand.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Recall: Who proposed that the planets orbit the Sun (heliocentric model) in the 1500s?
questions.answer: Nicolaus Copernicus
questions.explanation: Nicolaus Copernicus published the heliocentric model in 1543, placing the Sun at the center of planetary orbits.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Who first observed living cells under a microscope and called them 'animalcules'?
questions.answer: Antonie van Leeuwenhoek
questions.explanation: Antonie van Leeuwenhoek built powerful microscopes and was the first to observe bacteria and other microorganisms.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Which scientist developed the theory of relativity?
questions.answer: Albert Einstein
questions.explanation: Albert Einstein developed the special and general theories of relativity, transforming modern physics.

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Recall: Who formulated the laws of planetary motion?
questions.answer: Johannes Kepler
questions.explanation: Johannes Kepler formulated three laws describing how planets move in elliptical orbits around the Sun.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.answer: John Dalton

questions.subject: SCIENCE
questions.question: Who is credited with inventing the telephone?
questions.answer: Alexander Graham Bell

questions.subject: PSYCHOLOGY
questions.question: Which habit best protects your mind from being manipulated?

questions.explanation: Curiosity and evidence-checking are mental defenses that expose weak or dishonest claims.

questions.subject: PSYCHOLOGY
questions.question: A salesperson agrees with everything you say to seem like your 'twin.' Combined with fast urgency, this suggests ____.

questions.explanation: Excessive agreement plus pressure is a sales tactic; real relationships allow disagreement.

questions.explanation: Isolation removes outside perspectives that could expose the manipulator's behavior.

questions.question: Someone twists your words to attack an argument you never made. This fallacy is called ____.

questions.explanation: The straw man fallacy replaces your real position with a weaker fake version that is easier to attack.

questions.question: Which is TRUE about compliments from manipulators?

They are identical to honest praise
They are often strategic tools timed before requests

questions.question: Someone constantly compares you unfavorably to others to lower your confidence. This is ____.

questions.subject: PSYCHOLOGY
questions.question: A message claims 'Doctors hate this one trick!' to get clicks. This is ____.

questions.explanation: Sensational unsupported claims are clickbait; check reliable sources before believing them.

questions.question: Which is TRUE about healthy relationships versus manipulation?

questions.question: Which is a red flag in online group pressure?
choices: Members punish questioning with mockery or exclusion
questions.answer: Members punish questioning with mockery or exclusion
questions.explanation: Healthy groups tolerate questions; cult-like groups punish doubt to keep control.

Always agree to keep the peace

questions.explanation: Awareness and boundaries reduce exposure to people who weaponize your words.

questions.question: Which response shows assertive (not aggressive) resistance?
choices: 'I hear you, but my answer is no.'

questions.explanation: Assertiveness states your position clearly and respectfully without attack or surrender.

questions.question: A person copies your posture, phrases, and interests to quickly build fake trust. This tactic is called ____.

questions.question: Recall: A scammer claims to be a bank officer needing your OTP 'to protect your account.' You should ____.

Ask them to call later with the OTP

questions.explanation: One-time passwords are secrets; anyone asking for them is attempting fraud.

questions.question: What is the safest first step when an online message pressures you to act immediately?

questions.explanation: Pressure to act instantly is a red flag; verifying breaks the manipulation and protects you from scams.

questions.question: A rumor spreads fear: 'If you don't act now, something terrible will happen!' This uses ____.

questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.question: Which habit helps you bounce back faster after a bad day?
choices: A short wind-down routine: tidy space, reflect briefly, sleep on time
Replaying the day angrily for hours
questions.answer: A short wind-down routine: tidy space, reflect briefly, sleep on time
questions.explanation: Closure routines signal the brain that the day is done, protecting tomorrow's energy.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: PSYCHOLOGY
questions.question: A growth mindset believes that ____.
choices: Abilities can grow through effort and learning
questions.answer: Abilities can grow through effort and learning
questions.explanation: Growth mindset, researched by Carol Dweck, holds that effort and strategies develop ability over time.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: PSYCHOLOGY
questions.question: Self-compassion means ____.
choices: Excusing every mistake with no learning
Treating yourself with the same kindness you would offer a friend
questions.answer: Treating yourself with the same kindness you would offer a friend
questions.explanation: Self-compassion balances honesty with kindness, which research links to greater motivation and resilience.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: PSYCHOLOGY
questions.question: When grief or sadness feels overwhelming for weeks, the wise step is ____.

Talk to a trusted adult or counselor
Self-medicate with junk food or games
Wait years for it to pass alone
questions.answer: Talk to a trusted adult or counselor
questions.explanation: Persistent heavy feelings deserve professional support - reaching out is strength.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: PSYCHOLOGY
questions.question: The '3 good things' exercise builds resilience by ____.
choices: Training the brain to notice positives regularly
questions.answer: Training the brain to notice positives regularly
questions.explanation: Noting three good things daily rewires attention toward positives, improving mood over time.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: PSYCHOLOGY
questions.question: Which phrase best models resilient self-talk after a mistake?
choices: 'I made a mistake; what can I learn from it?'
questions.answer: 'I made a mistake; what can I learn from it?'
questions.explanation: Curious, kind self-talk after errors keeps you learning instead of spiraling.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: PSYCHOLOGY
questions.question: When a friend shares a problem, the most supportive first step is usually ____.
choices: Listen and acknowledge their feelings before offering advice
Tell them to stop being dramatic

questions.explanation: Feeling heard calms the nervous system; advice lands better after empathy.

questions.subject: PSYCHOLOGY
questions.question: Setting small achievable goals during hard times helps because ____.
choices: Small wins rebuild confidence and a sense of control
Success only comes from giant goals

questions.explanation: Achievable goals create momentum and prove to yourself that progress is possible.

choices: It shifts attention to positive aspects and builds emotional balance

questions.question: Which mindset helps when comparing yourself to others online?

Social media shows everyone's true worst

questions.explanation: Curated feeds distort comparison; measure progress against your own past self instead.

Immediately sharing your own worse story
Listening fully and asking what they need

questions.explanation: Support starts with presence and listening; advice comes only when wanted.

questions.subject: TECH 1
questions.question: If a component does not seat properly during assembly, you should ____.

questions.answer: Stop and check alignment; never force the part
questions.explanation: Forcing parts breaks connectors and boards; misalignment is the usual cause of resistance.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: TECH 1
questions.question: In the DMA procedure, what should you do while disassembling?
choices: Mix all screws in one pile
Document and organize every removed part and screw
Discard screws you cannot place immediately
questions.answer: Document and organize every removed part and screw
questions.explanation: Labeled parts and screws (often with photos) make correct reassembly possible.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: TECH 1
questions.question: Which is an ergonomic practice for computer work?
choices: Stare at a screen placed on the floor
Position the monitor at eye level and keep wrists straight while typing
questions.answer: Position the monitor at eye level and keep wrists straight while typing
questions.explanation: Ergonomics reduces eye strain and repetitive stress injuries during long sessions.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: TECH 1
questions.question: Which is the correct practice for handling a motherboard?
choices: Hold it by the edges, avoiding chips and contacts
Bend it slightly to check flexibility
Touch the gold contacts to test them
questions.answer: Hold it by the edges, avoiding chips and contacts
questions.explanation: Oils and static from hands can damage traces and contacts; edges are the safe grip points.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: TECH 1
questions.question: What should you do FIRST before opening any system unit?
choices: Open the case while it is running
Turn off the computer and unplug the power cord
questions.answer: Turn off the computer and unplug the power cord
questions.explanation: Working on a live system risks electric shock and component damage; always power down and unplug first.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: TECH 1
questions.question: Recall: Which OHS rule applies to compressed air cans?
choices: Inhale the spray to test it
Use near open flames for visibility
Use in short bursts, keep the can upright, and work in a ventilated area
questions.answer: Use in short bursts, keep the can upright, and work in a ventilated area
questions.explanation: Upright short bursts prevent propellant/liquid discharge; ventilation avoids inhaling propellant.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: TECH 1
questions.question: In DMA documentation, what does 'labeling cables before removal' prevent?
choices: Wrong reconnections that can damage components or stop the system from booting
questions.answer: Wrong reconnections that can damage components or stop the system from booting
questions.explanation: Labels (or photos) ensure each cable returns to its exact original header or port.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: TECH 1
questions.question: Recall: Which is a safe practice with power cables in a computer shop?
choices: Keep cords organized and away from walkways
Overload one outlet with many devices
questions.answer: Keep cords organized and away from walkways
questions.explanation: Organized, intact cords prevent tripping hazards, overloads, and shocks.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: TECH 1
questions.question: When cleaning inside a system unit, why should fans be held still while using compressed air?
choices: Fans will fly out of the case
Spinning fans from airflow can generate voltage and damage fan bearings or circuits
Holding them makes cleaning slower only
questions.answer: Spinning fans from airflow can generate voltage and damage fan bearings or circuits
questions.explanation: Letting compressed air overspin a fan can induce current back into the board and wear the bearing.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: TECH 1
questions.question: Recall: Which maintenance task helps prevent a system unit from overheating?
choices: Cleaning dust from fans, heatsinks, and vents
questions.answer: Cleaning dust from fans, heatsinks, and vents
questions.explanation: Dust insulates heat and blocks airflow; regular cleaning keeps cooling efficient.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: TECH 1
questions.question: Which tool is appropriate for blowing dust out of a system unit?
choices: Compressed air / blower used in short bursts
Wet cloth dripping inside the case
A household vacuum pressed against chips
questions.answer: Compressed air / blower used in short bursts
questions.explanation: Compressed air dislodges dust safely; vacuums can generate static and moisture causes shorts.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: TECH 1
questions.question: What is the safest way to carry a system unit?
choices: With both hands supporting the bottom, close to the body
questions.answer: With both hands supporting the bottom, close to the body
questions.explanation: Bottom support and a close grip prevent drops and back strain.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: TECH 1
questions.question: Why should you remove jewelry and metal watches before servicing a computer?
choices: Metal can cause short circuits and conduct static or current
It is only a dress code
questions.answer: Metal can cause short circuits and conduct static or current
questions.explanation: Conductive metal items can bridge circuits, creating shorts and shock paths.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: TECH 1
questions.question: Why is static electricity dangerous to computer parts?
choices: It only affects the case paint
It can silently damage sensitive chips and circuits

questions.explanation: ESD of even a few hundred volts can destroy microchips, often without visible signs.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: TECH 1
questions.question: Which OHS rule applies to eating areas in a technical shop?
choices: Drink soda near the solder station
Eat at the workbench between tasks
Eat only in designated areas away from chemicals and equipment
questions.answer: Eat only in designated areas away from chemicals and equipment
questions.explanation: Separating food zones prevents ingestion of solder, dust, and solvent residues.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: TECH 1
questions.question: Which sign warns of electrical hazard in a workshop?
choices: A yellow triangle with a lightning bolt symbol
questions.answer: A yellow triangle with a lightning bolt symbol
questions.explanation: Standard hazard signage (lightning bolt) marks areas or equipment with electrical danger.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.question: When two people must carry a long item (like a desk), they should ____.

Let the shorter person carry the heavy end

questions.explanation: Coordinated team lifting prevents sudden load shifts and back injuries.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: TECH 1
questions.question: What should be checked before re-connecting a serviced computer to power?

Connect power immediately to save time
Leave the case open for airflow during testing only if instructed and supervised
Skip the checklist if the parts look clean

questions.explanation: A pre-power checklist prevents short circuits from loose metal and mis-seated cables.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.subject: TECH 1
questions.question: A classmate spills water near a powered computer. The correct OHS action is ____.

Ignore it if the PC still runs
Shut down and unplug the unit, then dry and inspect before powering again
Wipe quickly while the PC stays on
questions.answer: Shut down and unplug the unit, then dry and inspect before powering again
questions.explanation: Water plus electricity equals shock and short risk; power down, dry thoroughly, and inspect first.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.explanation: Photos are fast, reliable documentation for correct reassembly.
questions.hint: Recall the lesson on this topic.

questions.question: Recall: Why are standoffs installed between the case and motherboard?

questions.subject: TECH 1
questions.question: A technician finds a swollen capacitor on a motherboard during maintenance. The correct action is ____.

Press the capacitor back into shape
Do not use the board; report/replace it, as swollen capacitors can fail or leak
questions.answer: Do not use the board; report/replace it, as swollen capacitors can fail or leak

choices: Align with the slot and press firmly straight down until the retention clip engages

choices: A thick layer covering the entire lid
A single tiny grain of sand only

questions.subject: TECH 1
questions.question: What does a long single beep (or beep code) at power-on usually indicate?
choices: A hardware issue reported by POST (meaning varies by BIOS brand)

Store the board socket-down on foam

questions.explanation: Bent LGA pins are a leading cause of dead boards; handle the socket area with care.

questions.question: Recall: When installing a CPU into an LGA socket, what should you do first?
choices: Apply paste to the socket pins
Lift the socket lever and align the notches before lowering the CPU
Press the CPU in at an angle
